candidates.name: Round-number stop cascades (Osler)
candidates.source: Osler, NY Fed Staff Reports 150 (2002, 'Stop-loss orders and price cascades') and 125 (2001, 'Currency orders and exchange-rate dynamics'), both read in full 2026-10-18; PDFs in marketdata/papers/
candidates.summary: After price crosses a 00 or 50 level (last two quoted digits) it keeps going for 1-2 hours, because stop-loss buys sit just above round numbers (01-10, 51-60) and stop-loss sells just below (90-99, 40-49), while take-profits sit exactly on 00. Touches without a cross reverse more often than at arbitrary levels. Test: enter in the cross's direction once price is k pips past the level, hold 15-120 minutes.
candidates.notes: Paper facts. SR150 (Reuters minute quotes, USD/DEM, USD/JPY, GBP/USD, New York 9:00-16:00, 1996-98): 'reach' = within 0.01% of the level; 'cross' = beyond it 15 minutes after reaching it (ex post, not tradeable as defined); moves signed in the approach direction. Table V, average move 15 min after a cross, round vs arbitrary levels: DEM 6.08 vs 5.37 bp, JPY 6.89 vs 5.98, GBP 4.92 vs 4.59 (excess +0.3 to +0.9 bp). Table VI.A, crossing minus reversing episodes: JPY +1.30 bp at 15 min, +1.34 at 30, +1.26 at 1 h, +2.35 at 2 h; DEM +1.12/+0.89/+0.57/+0.85; GBP +0.77/+0.80/+0.27/+0.35; negative at 1-2 days. Stronger after 12:30 New York (thinner market), no buy/sell asymmetry, weaker on 00-only levels, survives dropping BoJ intervention months. Large cascades about once a week vs about 5 round-number crosses a day, so the average is mostly ordinary crosses. Reversal on touch: round 58-60% vs arbitrary 55-57%. Order book (RBS, 9,667 orders, 1999-2000): stop-loss buys 14.4% at 01-10 vs 7.4% at 90-99, about 17-18% at 51-60 vs 6% at 40-49 (SR125's Table I prints the 50 rows in the other order, but its difference row and SR150's Table III agree); take-profits cluster exactly at 00; stops of $50m and over are 62% within 10 points of 00. SR125 adds a simulation only (order flow calibrated to the book reproduces both effects) and says the papers are 'silent on market efficiency... no attempt to evaluate risk-adjusted profits'. SR125 quotes the actual 30-min excess after a failed bounce as 0.0014% (0.14 bp) over 0.0063% for arbitrary levels, smaller still than SR150's tables. Prior: low. The gross edge is 0.3-2.4 bp, measured with an ex post cross; our USD/JPY cost is about 1.2 bp; the data are 25+ years old, from before algorithmic stop-running. Step 5-7 test spec (quant-coder, research/osler_round.py): USDJPY and EURUSD histdata M1 2009-2026 (marketdata/histdata/*_M1.csv.gz, bid quotes, so add the spread on entry); levels at 00 and 50 (JPY xx.00/xx.50, EUR 1.xx00/1.xx50), a 00-only variant; entry at the first M1 close k = 1, 3, 5 or 10 pips beyond a level after the price was on the other side within the last 15 minutes (a real-time cross); direction = the cross; exit after 15, 30, 60 or 120 minutes, or at a stop k pips back through the level; one trade per level per hour; sessions: all hours, London, New York, New York after 12:30 ET, no entries 21:00-23:00 UTC (rollover). Null: the same rule on arbitrary levels (10,000 random level grids shifted off 00/50, as in the papers); report round minus arbitrary per trade in bp, per 10-day block win count (binomial), and the reversal rate on touch. Pass to step 8 only if round minus arbitrary is positive in both halves (to 2017, from 2018) and the net Sharpe at 1.2 bp is >= 0.5 in both halves; then gates.py with 1.5x cost. Check overlap: correlation of daily returns with the breakout leg (USD/JPY London 10:00-18:00 server) and how many trades share its hours; rejected list has 'channel breakout', so a result that is just the generic breakout in disguise (arbitrary levels as good) is a fail. Result 2026-10-18 (research/osler_round.py, full run 710 s, USDJPY and EURUSD M1 2009-01 to 2026-10, 512 variants = 2 pairs x 2 level sets x k 1/3/5/10 x hold 15/30/60/120 x stop on/off x 4 sessions, 300 arbitrary grids each, costs 1.2 / 0.8 bp; trials line osler_round:grid count 512): REJECTED at steps 5-7. Step 5 data clean (no duplicates, 96-98% of weekday minutes, volatility peak at server 15:00 = 8:30 ET, so the clock is NY+7). No variant has net Sharpe >= 0.5 in both halves (0 of 512); the median gross per trade is negative (-0.46 / -0.22 bp) and the median round minus arbitrary is negative in both halves (-0.14 / -0.09 bp), so round levels do no better than arbitrary ones. Chosen on data to 2017: USDJPY 00-only, k=1, hold 120, no stop, NY after 12:30 ET: net Sharpe -0.16 to 2017, -0.69 from 2018; round minus arbitrary +0.86 then -0.46 bp; 10-day blocks 194/372 (p 0.22); 1.5x cost -0.53; correlation with the breakout leg -0.003, no shared hours. Reference k=3 / 30 min: gross -0.4 to +0.1 bp in every session, round at the 1st-89th percentile of arbitrary grids. Touch reversal goes against the paper on both pairs and in both halves: round 56-60% vs arbitrary 58-61% (-0.9 to -2.9 pp). Whatever SR150 saw in 1996-98 is not in 2009-26 M1 data, before or after costs.

candidates.name: AurumHydra margin-aware goal size cap
candidates.source: Decision 47 (2026-10-18): the round-5 margin model research/hydra_goal_margin_model.py and the tester's broker stop-outs in 7/10/9 of 21 months at 3x/4x/5x
candidates.summary: Choose InpGoalCap (now 50 in the target presets) so the goal sizing stops asking for sizes that end in a broker stop-out (margin level < 50%). Candidate caps are fixed sizes below the round-5 hit size (min 15, p5 20). The hit size is a ceiling and is never used as the cap value. Chosen on 2010-06..2017 month-start rounds, confirmed on 2018..2025-09, and the 21 tester months 2024.01-2025.09 are a check only. The cap is an existing input, so it is a preset value and needs no new EA code.
candidates.notes: Run 1 2026-10-18: research/hydra_size_cap.py (quant-coder), reusing the round-5 engine with the round-5 REDO fixes: C1 explicit no-clip branch returning 1.0 plus a five-parts unit test, fix parts clipped before cross parts in the same bar (Legs.mqh:1093-1098), boost extra haircut at edge 0.7, stated limits for noise P&L (round 4's constant ticket, NSXUSD M1 missing) and balance-vs-equity sizing. Result: all checks pass (copy check diff 0, round-5 replication 39.7/28.8/22.3, C1 PASS, unit tests PASS); with fixes 3+4 cap 50 gives 39.7/28.8/22.8% over 184 months. The rule picked cap 50 (the preset) at every goal: every static cap 3-14 loses 19-25 pp of P(goal) on 'to 2017' (3x all months: cap 14 20.7% vs 50 39.7%) for near-zero stop-outs. Cap 50 binds in 55/66/76% of rounds, and the median day-1 size asked is 36/43/47. Reviewer PASS WITH CHANGES: the conclusion covers caps <=14 only, not a static cap in general. Caps 15-49 were not tested (the hit size is a fixed-size stop-out level, not a bound on a capped schedule), so a static 20-45 test is a new pre-registered trial. The identity check is true by construction. The margin rates were fitted on the tester months' stop-outs (a broker measurement). Run 2 (next): a dynamic margin-aware cap that limits size so the margin level projected after the day's orders stays above a threshold fixed before the run; it must beat static caps 20-45 as well as 50. EA input off by default, judged in the tester on 2024.01-2025.09; model figures are an upper bound only. Run 2 2026-10-19: research/hydra_size_cap2.py (+ .out.txt, quant-coder), 12 variants pre-registered (static caps 20/25/30/35/40/45/50; dynamic min(50, s_dyn) at margin-level thresholds 1.5/2/3/4/6, OM_MAX = p95 of daily ticket margin to 2017 = 0.2337), chosen to 2017, confirmed 2018-2025.09. Checks 1-5 PASS (dyn off == cap 50 on 1104 rounds, s_dyn unit test, run-1 replication 39.7/28.8/22.8, holdout). Pick cap 50 at 3x/4x/5x: no variant better than the preset. Static: caps 20-40 trade P(goal) for fewer stop-outs steadily (3x to 2017: 27.5/31.9/38.5/39.6/42.9% vs 50 44.0%); cap 45 ties 50 at 3x (44.0/15.4) and misses the edge-0.7 floor at 4x by one month. Reviewer PASS WITH CHANGES: the static result stands, but the dynamic arm was degenerate by construction and is NOT a test of a margin-aware cap: it projected margin before the EA's 50% free-margin clip and summed all the day's tickets whether open together or not, so s_dyn <= 2.9 at every threshold (binds 100% of days, ~0% goal). 36 trials (63 with run 1, 60 unique). Run 3 (the last): a corrected dynamic cap â€” projected margin after the clip in the EA's order (hold, grid, tickets by open_ratio), leg margin as the peak of segments open together (legs_margin basis), thresholds near 1-2, a unit test running ea_day at s_dyn with no clip checking min open margin level >= thr on to-2017 days, and a degeneracy guard printed before the sweep (stop with no verdict if s_dyn binds on >90% or <5% of to-2017 days or its median is below 15). If it cannot be built cleanly, close the idea with cap 50 kept. Run 3 2026-10-19 (the last): research/hydra_size_cap3.py (+ .out.txt, quant-coder): clip-aware projection in the EA order (hold, grid, tickets via open_ratio; peak of open-together legs_margin; per-leg plan fitted to 2017, no look-ahead), thresholds 1.1/1.25/1.5/2/3 and degeneracy guard pre-registered. Checks 1-5 PASS (cap 50 reproduces 39.7/28.8/22.8; U2 engine agreement 276908 order-instant levels, 0 below thr). Guard: ALL DEGENERATE (bind 97.8-99.2% of 4281 to-2017 days, median bound s_dyn 3.0/2.0/1.2/0.1/0.0), no sweep, 0 new trials. Reviewer PASS WITH CHANGES: the degeneracy is real, not an artefact: the legs alone cap s_dyn(1.1) at about 0.909/0.128 = 7, and the projection differs from the engine only conservatively (grid before tickets, a full fresh grid, every leg every day), which would need a 6-8x smaller book to reach 15; the carried grid drives thr >= 2. The goal preset fits only through the 50% free-margin clip, so any margin-level cap above 1 is a static cap of about 0-3, which run 1 rejected. CLOSED: keep InpGoalCap 50, no tester job, no EA change. A sizing rule on another quantity would be a new candidate (reviewer does not recommend one).

candidates.name: AUD/USD break after Chinese macro releases (RBA 2016)
candidates.source: T. Mathews, The Effect of Chinese Macroeconomic News on Australian Financial Markets, RBA Bulletin Dec 2016, read in full 2026-10-19 (tools/pdf_text.py; PDF in marketdata/papers/)
candidates.summary: On scheduled China releases (GDP, activity, trade, CPI) take the 10-minute pre-release AUDUSD range; from the release to +60 min enter once per side on a break of it, stop at the other side, flat at +60 min or 06:00 server. AUDCAD as a second check. The direction is ours: the paper measures volatility only.
candidates.notes: Paper facts (Table A1, AUD/USD, extra absolute move in a 20-min window, -10 to +10 min, Thomson Reuters intraday, Jan 2000-Nov 2016, bootstrapped SEs): China GDP 0.01 / 0.06*** / 0.05*** % (2000-07 / 2008-16 / full); activity -0.01 / 0.04*** / 0.02**; trade 0.01* / 0.03***; CPI 0.03*** / 0.04*** / 0.01 (full n.s.); US labour force 0.16 / 0.20 / 0.18 for comparison. Rolling 5-year regressions: activity-day volatility about double the same-time normal by 2016; GDP, CPI, trade similar late in the sample. No surprise measure (no consensus series), no direction, no cost, no trading rule; GDP release times start 2003; the text warns of pre-release leaks (Orlik 2011), so the window starts 10 min early. Figures in docs/ideas/2026-10-18.md idea 1 match the PDF. Prior low-medium: 3-6 bp extra absolute move against about 1 bp round trip, but a breakout needs continuation after the first move, which the paper does not test; the rejected post-payroll/FOMC drift and channel breakout are the nearest families, so the test must report event days against same-time non-event days. Step 5 blocked on data: China release dates and times 2010-2025.09 (NBS GDP/activity/CPI, customs trade) are not in the repo; researcher to fetch (e.g. a dated economic-calendar archive with CNY events), then holdout.drop(). AUDUSD/AUDCAD M1 are in marketdata/histdata. Runs: 1 (2026-10-19, full read). Run 2 (2026-10-19, research/china_release_aud.py + .out.txt; researcher's NBS calendar marketdata/china_calendar_nbs.csv, 2015-2025.09 only, no trade, 220 events 57/163 by half): step 5 replicates the volatility for GDP and activity, not CPI (extra |move| -10..+10 min GDP 0.059/0.029 %, activity 0.044/0.027 %, CPI -0.012/-0.006 %; minute-profile peak at minute 0 in both halves, so the clock is right). Step 6-7 rule fixed before the run (10-min pre-range break, stop at the other side, flat at +60, 1.1 bp): AUDUSD net +0.099 / -0.017 R a trade (+0.23 / -0.24 bp), net Sharpe +0.30 / -0.06, event minus control +0.19 / +0.13 R per event with 90% CIs spanning 0; at 2.2 bp -0.06 / -0.19 R; AUDCAD -0.30 / -0.37 R. REJECTED at step 7: fails net R from 2018 and Sharpe >= 0.5 in both halves. The extra move is real but a breakout earns less than the spread. Per-series and narrow-range splits looked better but are diagnostics, not selected (narrow tercile 2018-on Sharpe 0.30 anyway). Control days gross +0.08-0.15 R before cost (bid-only fill-at-level bias, if any, favours the rule, so the rejection is not a bias artefact). 2 trials (docs/trials.jsonl china_release_aud:run2).
